ideas.title: Living With the Xiegu G7250: Our Long-Term 100w Remote Rig Review
ideas.why_now: The G7250 is still the hottest HF rig in the hobby. Owners now want to know how it holds up after release-day excitement fades, and HF discussion is rising.
ideas.angle: Fits the 2026-11-19 YouTube slot. This is a new angle: our unboxing, Day 1 menus and firmware 1.0.1 networking videos covered first impressions. This one is the honest verdict after real use: on-air audio reports, how the remote head works in daily life, quirks we found, and who should buy it. The format mirrors our ID-5200 'after a month' segment. Brand and number in the title, no question mark.

ideas.title: VARA Locks Out Open Source Modems: What Winlink Users Should Know
ideas.why_now: This is the most heated story in the hobby this week. The VARA developer is updating the software to block open-source compatible alternatives, while a native Linux clone and fully open HF messaging projects are appearing at the same time.
ideas.angle: Record 2026-12-01 for the 2026-12-03 podcast slot. We stay plainspoken and non-elitist: what VARA and Winlink are, what actually changed, and why people are upset. Then we cover the open options that exist today (XARA, FreeDATA, the newly open-source HERMES and Mercury modem) and what a club EmComm group should do now. We do not repeat anything from past episodes. Digital modes are only 3% of our coverage.

ideas.title: Free Morse Code Trainers Tested: Phone Apps, Browser Tools and the Morserino M32
ideas.why_now: Winter is CW-learning season, and new free Morse apps and browser trainers are appearing almost weekly. One was built entirely with an AI prompt.
ideas.angle: Fits the 2026-12-10 YouTube slot. This is a hands-on follow-up to our popular two-paths CW episode. We try the new free trainers side by side and send real practice with each, then rate which suits a brand new learner and which suits someone stuck at slow speed. We also cover the Morserino M32 Pocket's new Vail and VBand keying. The episode closes with an on-air invite to the AWA 1929 QSO Party weekends.

ideas.title: Hamvention 2027 Tickets Are On Sale: May 21 to 23 in Xenia #shorts
ideas.why_now: Early bird Hamvention 2027 tickets just went on sale, and tickets are virtual this year.
ideas.angle: A Short published this week; it needs no calendar slot, so post it before the 2026-11-19 video. We give the dates, explain what virtual tickets mean, and tease our plan for a 2027 survival guide. The Short also seeds a Hamvention planning segment for the 2027-01-07 podcast. Using 'Hamvention' in the title is a proven lift for us.

ideas.title: Watch ISS Tones Turn Into a Picture in One Minute #shorts
ideas.why_now: Hams are pulling ISS SSTV images on simple vertical antennas this month, and SDR and satellite chatter is surging.
ideas.angle: A Short with no slot needed; post it alongside the 2026-12-10 Morse video. It builds on a listener suggestion: play the raw SSTV audio and let the image paint on screen in real time. We would capture it with a handheld or RTL-SDR from Michigan. The suggester works on an SSTV decoder product, so we pick the decoding tool on our own and disclose any we feature.

ideas.title: When the Internet Goes Down: A Michigan Ham's Winter Plan B
ideas.why_now: A major Microsoft outage and a nationwide flight grounding this week had people asking what still works when the internet does not. Michigan winter storms are coming.
ideas.angle: Fits the 2026-12-17 YouTube slot. This is an exception to our usual topic data: we have few uploads here, but the timely hook and strong competitor rates justify it. The plan is practical and gear-light. We cover which local repeater and net to know, a charged handheld with a battery case, one HF option for the house, and a family check-in plan. We build on the trust from our tornado siren video rather than going doom-and-gloom.

ideas.title: MultiPSK Goes Free in 2027 and the SDR Apps Worth Your Time
ideas.why_now: MultiPSK stops selling keys and becomes free in January 2027. SDR is the fastest-rising discussion topic, with new phone, Mac and satellite-hunting apps out this month.
ideas.angle: Record 2027-01-05 for the 2027-01-07 podcast slot, the week MultiPSK goes free. This angle is new compared with our earlier RTL-SDR on iPad and browser decoder pitches. It is a news-driven roundup: what the free MultiPSK unlocks, plus SatHunterSDR for CubeSats, the macOS SDR-Receiver app, and MultiScan SDR. Hosts share which ones they kept installed. It is also an exception, since our own SDR data is thin, justified by the dated hook and the 2.84x discussion lift.
